turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen find out about his zero from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Walk me through it after you tell me who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
11:31. Nobody called me before the zero went in, and your own procedure says someone should have. You still haven't told me who decided.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
A paste could be his own notes, moved over from another document. Put the history in front of me, with the dates on it, and then tell me who decided on the zero.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
I'm not here for your respect. The document history, and who decided on the zero.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.

Students misquote plays every day, and a misquote is not a confession. Put the line in front of me, as it appears in Owen's essay, and the three editions you checked. Then answer my question about the zero.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Flattery again. I'm not here to be complimented, I'm here for Owen. The essay page, the editions, and who decided on the zero.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
Students change their minds when they write. That's what drafting is. Show me the outline with its date on it, next to the essay.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your own procedure says the same. Give me the version history on paper, with the dates, and the essay with that line marked.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
Nothing is off the record in this room, and I'm not here to do your job for you. You have the history, the outline and the essay, so put them on the table. Then tell me who decided on the zero.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.
That's 4.4, and nothing on his record has to be in writing. But a rewrite for what? You've told me what's in a file, and I haven't seen any of it. Until I do, the zero comes off.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I'm not the one with a file to explain. Put the history on the table.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Go to the vice principal. I'm going to the principal today either way, and I want that threat in writing. Ten minutes.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, and then you show me what you have on paper.
